# Ca-EDTA Complex Dissociation

## Setting Up the Problem

The formation reaction is:
$$\text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{EDTA}^{4-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca-EDTA}^{2-}$$

with formation constant:
$$K_f = \frac{[\text{Ca-EDTA}]}{[\text{Ca}^{2+}][\text{EDTA}]} = 5 \times 10^{10}$$

## Analyzing the Dissociation

Since we start with a stoichiometric complex, the dissociation produces equal amounts of Ca²⁺ and EDTA:

$$\text{Ca-EDTA} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{EDTA}$$

Let x = [Ca²⁺] = [EDTA] at equilibrium

Since K_f is very large, dissociation is minimal, so:
$$[\text{Ca-EDTA}] \approx 0.02 \text{ M}$$

## Solving

$$K_f = \frac{[\text{Ca-EDTA}]}{[\text{Ca}^{2+}][\text{EDTA}]} = \frac{0.02}{x^2} = 5 \times 10^{10}$$

Solving for x²:
$$x^2 = \frac{0.02}{5 \times 10^{10}} = 4 \times 10^{-13}$$

$$x = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-13}} = 6.3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ M}$$

## Verification

The dissociation (6.3×10⁻⁷ M) is negligible compared to 0.02 M, so our approximation is valid. ✓

Answer: D
